correctness.rationale: For a tagged proposed object at time s, exact rejection requires two accepted predecessors in its exclusion neighbourhood E with different colors. A bounded Minkowski-expanded dependency set U=E+E makes probability of >=3 earlier proposals O(s^3); the two-point Poisson term has factor r^2 s^2/2, accounting for temporal order. If predecessor centers mutually conflict (measure T(E)), they must take opposite colors under both rules; otherwise random independent available colors reject with probability 1/2 while first-available priority accepts. Hence F_random=r^2 s^2 (|E|^2+T)/4+O(s^3), F_priority=r^2 s^2 T/2+O(s^3). Campbell/Poisson insertion integration yields rho_random=rt-r^3t^3(|E|^2+T)/12+O(t^4), rho_priority=rt-r^3t^3T/6+O(t^4), and the claimed difference. Independent geometry: rods E=(-sigma,sigma) have |E|^2=4sigma^2,T=3sigma^2; independently numerically integrated disk intersection and recovered T/sigma^4=pi^2-3sqrt(3)pi/4 to 35+ digits. The exact Poisson factorial expansion establishes the continuum statement; sampling and numerical quadrature are corroborative only.

value.rationale: An explicit nonzero cubic coefficient decisively invalidates a stated exact total-density equivalence between randomly selected and priority-selected colors in a continuum adsorption model. The general bounded symmetric exclusion-set formula and closed rod/disk constants quantify the first physical order of discrepancy and can correct perturbative density modeling. The result is local at short time, not an all-time jamming or density-order theorem.
